variantPolicy: Seeded defect signals vary replay context but are not independent published assets or assessment items.

exercises.title: Repair Extension Wiring with a Red-Green Test Pair
exercises.objective: Diagnose a missing extension/Spring dependency and define separate fast unit and platform context tests before accepting the repair.

initialState.defect: academyfacades declares a bean whose constructor requires academyCoreService, but extensioninfo.xml omits the core extension dependency.
initialState.observedFailure: Application context creation reports no qualifying academyCoreService bean.

exercises.prompt: Produce the minimal dependency repair and a red-green test plan. Include a Mockito unit test for facade delegation and a platform context/integration test that proves the actual extension graph and Spring bean load. Explain which test can run without Commerce and which requires the JUnit tenant/runtime. Record the failing signal, command/report artifact, expected negative case, and passing evidence; do not claim live execution.
constraints: Do not add unrelated global extensions.
Do not call an ordinary Mockito test a platform integration test.
No licensed SAP Commerce runtime is available in this repository.
acceptanceCriteria: Identifies the missing declared extension dependency.
Isolates facade behavior with a mock in the unit test.
Uses a platform context test for real Spring/extension wiring.
Includes a negative context-load signal and passing rerun evidence.
Labels platform execution as required but unavailable locally.
Names the targeted test command/report without claiming it ran.

hints.text: A Mockito test can prove delegation but cannot prove localextensions/extensioninfo or the platform application context.
Require one red context-load observation before the manifest repair and one green report after it in a real Commerce test environment.

exercises.referenceSolution: Add the precise academycore dependency, retain constructor injection, and write a fast Mockito facade test for delegation and failure propagation. Add a platform integration/context test under testsrc that loads the actual bean and asserts its dependency is resolvable. Capture the pre-fix context failure and post-fix targeted test report in a licensed runtime. This academy evaluates the plan and defect diagnosis only.
exercises.executionBoundary: The academy executes deterministic rubric validation only; the platform context test requires a configured SAP Commerce JUnit tenant and was not run here.

exercises.title: Expose a Broken Relation with Persistence Integration Tests
exercises.objective: Correct a relation cardinality/uniqueness defect and prove persisted behavior, rejection, cleanup, and query semantics in the platform test runtime.

initialState.defect: ComplianceDocument.code is treated as globally unique although business identity is catalogVersion plus code; a relation also permits the same document to be assigned twice.
initialState.failure: Importing the same code in Staged and Online violates the generated persistence constraint.

exercises.prompt: Redesign the identity and relation, then specify a transactional platform integration test using version-appropriate SAP Commerce base-test infrastructure. Test Staged/Online coexistence, duplicate rejection within one catalog version, relation uniqueness, FlexibleSearch retrieval, and cleanup/isolation. Separate any pure mapper/unit tests from tests requiring generated models, type metadata, database persistence, and the JUnit tenant. Include red and green result evidence without claiming execution here.
constraints: Do not solve the defect by removing every uniqueness invariant.
Do not use an in-memory POJO test as proof of Commerce persistence behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Defines composite business identity semantics.
Tests two catalog versions and same-version duplicates.
Verifies relation uniqueness and FlexibleSearch retrieval.
Uses isolated deterministic data and cleanup/transaction behavior.
Distinguishes generated-model/database tests from pure unit tests.
Records target update line, runner mode, command, report, and unavailable local execution.

hints.text: A Java equals assertion cannot prove generated deployment constraints or catalog-version persistence.
The negative test should fail for a same-version duplicate while allowing the same code in another catalog version.

exercises.referenceSolution: Model identity as catalogVersion plus code at the service/import contract and use relation modifiers that prevent duplicate assignment without erasing legitimate cross-version records. In the target update line, use the verified transactional SAP Commerce integration base, create isolated catalog versions and documents, assert cross-version success and same-version rejection, query persisted state, and verify rollback/cleanup. Run and capture this only in a configured platform test environment.
exercises.executionBoundary: Generated models, type metadata, FlexibleSearch, and persistence require the SAP Commerce JUnit tenant; this repository does not execute those platform tests.

exercises.title: Test Transaction Rollback and External Compensation
exercises.objective: Repair a service that performs a remote reservation inside a local transaction and verify rollback, idempotency, retry, and reconciliation behavior.

initialState.defect: placeOrder saves local order state, calls inventory remotely, then throws before commit; an automatic retry can reserve inventory twice.
initialState.failure: The database rolls back but the first remote reservation remains.

exercises.prompt: Propose a safe service boundary and a test-first repair. Include fast Mockito unit tests for call ordering and failure propagation, a transactional platform integration test for local rollback, and a fault-injection/contract test for timeout-after-remote-success and duplicate retry. Define an idempotency or reconciliation mechanism, negative cases, deterministic fixtures, and red/green execution artifacts. State which evidence cannot be produced without SAP Commerce and the external test double.
constraints: Do not assume a database rollback reverses a remote side effect.
Do not hide the failure with an unbounded retry.
Do not execute learner-submitted code on the academy host.
acceptanceCriteria: Separates local atomic state from remote effects.
Tests rollback after an injected local failure.
Tests timeout after remote success and duplicate delivery.
Asserts idempotency key or reconciliation outcome.
Uses mocks only for isolated unit behavior and a platform runtime for persistence/transaction proof.
Records commands, reports, and observed state without false execution claims.

hints.text: Inject a failure both before and after the remote system has accepted the reservation; those cases require different assertions.
The platform test proves local transaction behavior. A service-virtualization test proves the ambiguous remote outcome and deduplication contract.

exercises.referenceSolution: Persist an explicit pending operation or outbox/idempotency record within the local transaction, perform the remote effect outside the local atomic boundary, and reconcile ambiguous outcomes by durable key. Unit-test orchestration and failures with mocks; platform-test local rollback and persisted operation state; contract-test remote accepted-then-timeout and duplicate requests. Preserve red/green reports from the appropriate environments.
exercises.executionBoundary: Local transaction semantics require a configured SAP Commerce test tenant; remote ambiguity requires an isolated mock server or service virtualizer. Neither runtime exists here.

exercises.title: Break and Secure an OCC Ownership Check
exercises.objective: Repair an endpoint that authenticates a caller but fails resource-ownership authorization, and prove its contract through layered negative tests.

initialState.defect: GET /users/{userId}/orders/{code} checks for a valid token but loads any order code without proving ownership.
initialState.defectiveImplementation: OrderData get(String userId, String code) { return facade.getOrderDetails(code); }
initialState.failure: Customer A can request Customer B's order when the code is known.

exercises.prompt: Design the controller/facade ownership repair and a layered test suite: isolated authorization-policy unit test, controller validation/error mapping test, API contract test, and platform web/integration test in the target Commerce update line. Include unauthenticated, wrong-user, malformed identifier, nonexistent resource, permitted support-role, success, and information-disclosure assertions. Record test commands/reports and explain that no live OCC endpoint was executed here.
constraints: Do not leak resource existence through inconsistent forbidden/not-found behavior without an explicit policy.
Do not embed answer keys or credentials in client-visible fixtures.
acceptanceCriteria: Enforces server-side ownership or authorized support-role access.
Covers unauthenticated, unauthorized, malformed, absent, and success cases.
Asserts stable status/error schema and no sensitive body leakage.
Separates ordinary controller/unit tests from platform web integration.
Includes deterministic identities and cleanup.
Records target version, command, report, and unexecuted local boundary.

hints.text: Test two distinct customers and one explicitly authorized support principal; a single happy-path identity cannot expose the defect.
Assert response body and timing/error consistency as well as status codes so the endpoint does not become an order-enumeration oracle.

exercises.referenceSolution: Resolve the authenticated principal server-side and enforce ownership or an explicit support permission before mapping order data. Keep the policy below the UI/controller convenience layer. Use unit tests for policy branches, controller tests for validation/error mapping, contract tests for stable schemas, and target-version platform web integration tests for security filters and wiring. Capture failures before the repair and passing reports after it only in authorized test environments.
exercises.executionBoundary: The academy validates the test design and security reasoning; actual OCC filter-chain and platform web integration tests require the target SAP Commerce runtime.
